testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is okay to have a missing lug nut if at least four other lug nuts are present on the rim.
A cracked lock ring is safe if the vehicle drives under 55 mph.
A missing clamp is dangerous and needs to be fixed.
Welded wheel repairs are safe for rear axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp is dangerous and needs to be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Bent or cracked lock rings are not safe. Welded wheel repairs are not safe.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often use curved, convex mirrors. Convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes activate?

options.text: You cannot move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks automatically refill themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. This tank can be used to temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be parked at the end of an exercise?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
Within five feet of where the examiner said.
Wherever it is safe to park.
Within two feet of where the examiner said.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle exactly where the examiner instructed. Not parking in the exact spot can result in points lost or failure on the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should you do with cargo inside a trailer?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
Stack it no higher than three feet.
Secure it so it does not move during driving.
Put the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it so it does not move during driving.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured to prevent movement while driving. Loose cargo is dangerous to you and other drivers.

questions.question: If you feel tired before driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Take caffeine pills.
Do not drive.
Drive as fast as possible to reach your destination quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive.
questions.explanation: Caffeine pills and coffee cannot prevent fatigue. They may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. When you feel tired, you need sleep. The only solution is to stop driving and rest.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.

options.text: Double clutching
Double shifting
Triple clutching
Triple shifting

questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching. Release the gas and push in the clutch while shifting to neutral. After releasing the clutch and letting the vehicle reach the right speed, push in the clutch again, shift gears, then release the clutch and accelerate.

questions.question: Why should you use caution with flares after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.
Flares are expensive.
Other drivers may become confused.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Spilled fuel and improper flare use can cause a fire after an accident.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you approach the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Always keep both hands on the steering wheel when turning quickly to avoid a hazard. A firm grip helps you turn the wheel fast enough.

questions.question: Why do you need to drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
To allow for changes in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil build up over time and can damage the brakes. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: You should use at least ____ tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.

options.text: One tie-down
Two tie-downs
Three tie-downs
Four tie-downs

questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo needs at least two tie-downs, even if it is small.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A type of warning system
A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part within the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.correctAnswerText: A type of warning system
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items covering the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include drivers who have not scraped ice from windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to limited rear visibility. Simply operating a pick-up truck is not inherently hazardous.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting livestock, drivers should be concerned about:

options.text: Other motorists seeing the livestock.
The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.
Extra tolls.
Passing emissions testing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's weight shifting as the animals move.
questions.explanation: Live animals lean during curves and move around during transit. This makes the weight distribution unstable. Driving with livestock requires extra care.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine compartment, you should not:

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Drain the brake fluid.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the engine compartment, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. Do not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a serious traffic violation?

options.text: Excessive speeding.
Littering.
Reckless driving.
Following too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Littering.
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include excessive speeding, reckless driving, operating a truck without a valid CDL, following too closely, and improper lane use. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your license. Littering is not a serious traffic violation.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Switch lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and speed. Check your mirrors and look in all directions while on the expressway.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ensure that the truck is not overloaded.
Ensure that the cargo is balanced.
Ensure that the cargo is secured properly.
Ensure that the breakable items are placed under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the breakable items are placed under heavier items.
questions.explanation: Inspect cargo to make sure it is properly secured, balanced, and does not exceed weight limits. Do not place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:

options.text: Speed.
Sunshine.
Time of day.
Traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by driving speed, vehicle weight, and road surface conditions.

questions.question: How is water and compressor oil removed from the bottom of an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out of the tank.
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
The water and oil are removed automatically as the brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil are removed from air storage tanks by opening a drain valve. If this buildup is left in the system, it can damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
Stack it no more than three feet high.
Secure it to prevent movement.
Load heavier items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to prevent it from moving during transport. Arrange cargo to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and evenly distributed.

questions.question: When do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: Only after the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
After other road surfaces freeze.
Before other road surfaces.
They have heaters to prevent freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Drive carefully when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, what must you do?

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Do not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and always maintain three points of contact. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic test failure.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers or trailers without sides must be tied down to prevent it from shifting or falling off during transport.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle's engine runs without oil?

options.text: The vehicle will likely run smoothly.
The vehicle will make quick jerks while driving.
The engine may be damaged quickly.
Gas mileage will improve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: An engine can be severely damaged very quickly without oil. Do not operate a vehicle if its oil pressure gauge is low or fluctuating.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long when shifting gears?

options.text: The vehicle will speed up.
You may have trouble getting into the next gear.
You may kill the engine.
The vehicle will be difficult to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble getting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral for too long when shifting may make it difficult to put the vehicle into the next gear.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a problem with an exhaust system?

options.text: Loose or broken exhaust pipes
Loose or broken mounting brackets
Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: When inspecting an exhaust system, check that parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: What is true about pull-ups during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
Some test administrators accept excessive pull-ups.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, a pull-up occurs when you stop and pull forward to gain a better position. Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: What should you do when turning to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not brake because it could lock the wheels.
Turn the wheel very sharply.
Hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not apply the brakes while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Ability to focus
Daydreaming
Yawning repeatedly
Drifting from your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: How can you best avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Wear sunglasses.
Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look to the right side of the road.
Use your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, glance toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: Why is driving too fast dangerous?

options.text: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
It is a good way to reach your destination quickly.
It should only be done on dry roads.
It is acceptable when traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many fatal crashes. Never drive above the speed limit. Always adjust your speed to match road conditions.

questions.question: What kind of force must emergency brakes use in an air brake system?

options.text: Air pressure
Mechanical
Heavy
Electrical

questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to hold the brakes on.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Move quickly to get out of other drivers' way.
Avoid using your mirrors.
Start from any position.
Use a helper if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: Backing up a large truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper when possible.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a long trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
Drive alone.
Schedule long trips at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on a long trip, get enough sleep before you leave. Plan your route and stopping points ahead of time. Drive with a passenger. Drive during times when you are normally awake.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time, emphasizing different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.
By someone other than the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important items and makes it less likely you will forget something.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce driving distractions?

options.text: Pre-programming radio stations
Planning your route before driving
Eating while driving
Adjusting mirrors before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Eating while driving
questions.explanation: To avoid distractions, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for one of two reasons. Which is one of them?

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pressure
You are driving uphill.
The brakes get too cold.
The brakes are used too much in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of hydraulic pressure
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failures happen for two main reasons. The first is overusing brakes on a downgrade, which causes them to fade. The second is loss of hydraulic pressure in the system. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.

questions.question: When brakes fade on a steep downgrade, what happens?

options.text: They become quieter.
They become less effective.
They work better than usual.
They work differently from front to back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downgrade causes them to overheat and become less effective. To prevent brake overheating on a hill, use engine braking instead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Change quickly before other vehicles can enter the lane.
Change slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
Not use a turn signal.
Avoid the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. If another vehicle is in the lane and you did not see it, the driver will have more time to react to your vehicle.

questions.question: To park as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave.
So that you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. When possible, park so you can pull forward to exit the space.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Not drive in any lane.
Wait until construction is done before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In work zones, drive at the posted speed limit. Slow down more when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet.
Within 1,000 feet.
Within the distance you can see ahead.
Immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive so you can stop completely within the area of road you can see ahead of you.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.
Start the vehicle.
Tap the accelerator twice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, pull the knob to apply the parking brake and push it in to release it.

questions.question: During a written exam:

options.text: Cell phones can be on airplane mode.
Cell phones must be off.
Cell phones can be on if placed face down.
Cell phones can be on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cell phones must be off.
questions.explanation: All electronic devices must be turned off during a written exam.

questions.question: If a driver operates in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license type should they choose?

options.text: Either excepted or non-excepted.
Excepted.
Non-excepted.
Traditional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Non-excepted.
questions.explanation: To operate in both types of intrastate commerce, you must choose a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is important, especially at night.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you that you are braking?

options.text: Tap the brakes a few times.
Stick your arm out the window.
Swerve within your lane.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a few times.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.

options.text: Single.
Dual.
Triple.
Quad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.
